newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan says peace process in "real crisis".
newsitem.headline: Jordan says peace process in "real crisis".

text.p: Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti said on Tuesday the Middle East peace process was in crisis because of Israeli plans for Jewish settlements and its limited withdrawal from the West Bank.

"We believe the peace process is passing through a very real crisis. We warn against any unilateral action would present us with difficult choices," Kabariti told reporters after talks with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
Kabariti echoed comments made on Monday by Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, who also said the peace process was in real crisis.

"I affirmed to the Israeli minister that Israel, with its unilateral decisions, either over settlements or on the scale of the redeployment, has put the Palestinians in a great predicament, whose results (the Palestinians) have to bear alone," Kabariti said. "Jordan rejects these decisions."
Kabariti said King Hussein had sent Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu two messages setting out Jordan's concern over the Israeli moves.
Mordechai tried to play down tension between the two sides after his meeting with Kabariti. "There were some misunderstandings but I am sure we can overcome those problems," he said.
